title: delurio binding (binding.yaml, <name>.binding.yaml)
description: How a flow, or a navigation graph, maps onto a running app, for replay and recording (SPEC.md §7). A binding may `extends` a shared one, which may leave out what the bindings that extend it give. The keys are those the replay reads; what they name in the graph (a state, a node, an event, a scenario) is checked when a replay loads the binding (`replay --check`).
$comment: a binding with nav, setup, personas, frames, pages or entries binds a navigation graph; any other, a flow

kind.description: The kind of graph file. A binding is `binding`.

extends.description: A shared binding this one extends, relative to it: its keys come first, and the maps (apps, data, accounts, scenarios, …) are merged key by key.

root.description: The folder commands run in, relative to the binding's file; its folder when left out.

apps.description: Each app's base address, used as {<app>} in addresses.

width.description: The window's width in CSS pixels (1280).

height.description: The window's height in CSS pixels (720).

locale.description: The BCP 47 tag the browser is set to; every screen is read against the flow's catalog of that language.

timezone.description: The IANA time zone the browser is set to.

timeout.description: How many seconds a step waits at most (10).

ignoreHTTPSErrors.description: true: a page served with a certificate no authority signed opens all the same.

data.description: Sources of values, each a JSON or dotenv file, used as {<source>.<path>}; read when a walk starts, after its setup, and again after each command. Secrets in them are masked in reports.

additionalProperties.$comment: a source is { json: <path> } or { dotenv: <path> }

signIn.description: How an account signs in: the actions, with the account's fields as {placeholders}. It signs in whoever acts, so no action carries `as`.

accounts.description: The people a walk acts as, each with the fields signIn and the steps use as {placeholders}.

samples.description: Values for the sample placeholders of the graph's texts (a flow) or the :params of the routes (a navigation graph).

quiet.description: How many milliseconds the page is still before a screen is read (400).

max.description: How many milliseconds a screen waits for that at most: browser.timeout, which it never passes.

settle.description: When a screen is read: once the page has been still for `quiet` ms, waiting at most `max` ms.

parallel.description: Walks at once: true (as many as the machine holds), a number from 1 to 16, auto, or { walks, serial }, where each serial group names scenarios or accounts (a navigation graph's personas or accounts) whose walks share something fixed and go one after another. false: one at a time.

open.description: An address a signed-in person opens.

find.description: What only a signed-in page shows.

maxAge.description: How long a saved sign-in lasts: 30m, 12h, 2d, or a number of seconds (12h).

fresh.description: Scenarios (a navigation graph's personas) or accounts that always sign in anew.

session.description: A sign-in through signIn is kept and reused across runs once checked.

flow.description: The id of the flow it binds.

mask.description: The sensitivities of the domain's fields (credential, personal, internal) whose nodes a recording, a video made from it and a replay's screenshots blur: [credential] when left out, [credential, personal] for an app whose data is real, [] for nothing (a tutorial filmed with a password made up for it).

pageErrors.description: An error the page leaves uncaught fails the walk (`fail`, the default), or is only listed (`report`).

save.description: Run after a scenario's setup and sign-in.

restore.description: Run in place of the setup on the scenario's later walks.

drop.description: Run once for each snapshot when the replay ends.

snapshot.description: A scenario's setup run once, kept, and given back to its later walks: commands only.

given.description: Where the walk starts: a value for each context variable the flow starts with `initial: any`.

as.description: The account whose browser the walk is in.

signIn.description: false: the account is not signed in through signIn first.

open.description: The address the walk starts at.

vars.description: Values for {placeholders} of this scenario's walks. A var is not named like a field of an account the scenario acts as.

samples.description: Values for the sample placeholders of the graph's texts, over the binding's samples.

then.description: How the steps that leave a variable to chance (havoc) come out on this scenario's walks, by the effect: a list read in order, one entry each time the walk takes a transition that applies the effect, each entry a value for some of the variables the effect's havoc lists. A variable an entry leaves out, and every variable once the list has run out, keeps its value. Proposed on 23 Nov 2026.

setup.description: Commands run before the walk, such as seeding the database: run only.

teardown.description: Commands run after the walk: run only.

javaScript.description: false: the walk's browser runs no JavaScript, through the pages marked `script`.

viewport.description: The walk's window, instead of the binding's browser width and height: a phone's.

enter.description: How the scenario's walk comes into the flow after it opens its page: by an entry of a navigation graph ({ nav, bind, entry }), or from another flow that starts this one ({ flow, bind, given, event }). Paths are relative to the binding's file.
enter.$comment: enter by a nav entry with nav, else from a flow

bind.description: Its binding; may be left out when the entry's label alone finds it.

given.description: Where the other flow starts: its context.

event.description: The event of the transition whose `starts` names this flow.

additionalProperties.description: How a walk starts: where (`given`), as whom, on which page, after what setup.

events.description: The actions that cause an event no node on screen sends, by event.

url.description: A glob the page's address matches in this state (* is one path segment, ** anything).

reach.description: A scenario whose shortest drivable path reaches this state, for a tutorial's `cut`.

call.description: The server call the state makes: its URL glob, or { url, method, action, code, returns, status }. Held while the state's own screen is checked, and its HTTP status compared with the refusal's on a FAIL.<class> walk. On a state that invokes none of the flow's actions, a request the page makes while the state is shown, such as one to another server; status is then the HTTP status its answer has.

url.description: The URL glob the call goes to (a server action: the page's own address).

action.description: The server action's id, as its Next-Action header carries it (a text between slashes is a regular expression), or true for any server action posted there.

code.description: The path of the refusal code in what the call returned.

returns.description: By DONE or a FAIL event of the state: what the call returned, { path, equals } or { text }.

path.description: Keys and indexes in what it returned.

text.description: A text its answer holds. A text between slashes is a regular expression.

status.description: On a state that invokes none of the flow's actions: the HTTP status the call's answer has, or a list of those it may have. Proposed on 23 Nov 2026.

storage.description: What the page's storage holds when the state is checked: session (sessionStorage) and local (localStorage), of the origin of the page the state is shown on, in the browser whose screen it is. Proposed on 23 Nov 2026.

session.description: By key glob (* any run of characters): absent, no key it matches is there; any other value, a key it matches is there and each it matches holds that value (a text with {placeholders}, or a regular expression between slashes).

local.description: By key glob (* any run of characters): absent, no key it matches is there; any other value, a key it matches is there and each it matches holds that value (a text with {placeholders}, or a regular expression between slashes).

fail.description: FAIL.<class> → how the held call is made to fail on a walk that leaves the state so, where the context does not cause it. Needs `call`.

additionalProperties.description: How the held call is made to fail: abort (no answer, or { abort: <network error> }), { status, body, contentType, headers } (an answer the replay gives instead of the server), hang (no answer while the walk is at the state) or signOut (the session ends and the call goes on without its credentials).

body.description: The answer's text; {placeholders} are filled as in every binding string.

as.description: The account whose screen this state is: it is checked, and its nodes pressed, in that person's context.

before.description: Done when the walk reaches the state, before it is checked.

additionalProperties.description: What a replay checks of a state beyond its nodes, and the call it holds.

allOf.$comment: fail makes the state's call fail, so it needs call

frame.description: The CSS selector of the iframe the element is drawn in, such as a payment provider's hosted form; looked in first.

name.description: With role: its accessible name. A text between slashes is a regular expression.

text.description: The text it shows. A text between slashes is a regular expression.

label.description: The label of a form control. A text between slashes is a regular expression.

hasText.description: Of what the rest finds, those that hold this text. A text between slashes is a regular expression.

within.description: Looked for inside what this locator finds.

nth.description: Of what the rest finds, this one: from 0, the first; a negative one counts from the end, -1 the last.

before.description: Done before the node is pressed, such as opening the menu it sits in.

count.description: How many elements its locator finds: a number, or a value of the data ("{data.path}").

near.description: The element this node is drawn beside: in every state that shows the node, each element its locator finds is at most 24 CSS pixels from the one element this locator finds (0 where they overlap). Proposed on 23 Nov 2026.

draws.description: Another flow's screen that this node holds, drawn by something other than that flow's own page: the node's locator finds the one element that holds it, and the replay checks the drawn flow's nodes inside it, for the state that `states` maps each state to, or its first screen. Paths are relative to the binding's file. Proposed on 23 Nov 2026.

bind.description: Its binding, where its nodes are found by its own `nodes`.

given.description: The drawn flow's context, for the variables its screens read that start from any value.

states.description: By state of this flow that shows the node: the state of the drawn flow whose screen it holds.

additionalProperties.description: Where the replay finds a node that its role and name cannot find, what it does before pressing it, how many elements it finds, what it is drawn beside, another flow's screen it holds, or that it is skipped.

allOf.$comment: draws finds the element that holds the drawn screen by the node's own locator

effects.description: By flow effect, or domain action a state invokes: the checks of what a step changes outside the screen, run after a walked transition applies it (typically `run` with `expect`).

find.description: The open menu, where its entries are found.

file.description: A fixture, or a list of them, each relative to the binding's file and inside its folder.

run.description: A helper and its arguments, run with no shell: its output is the file.

fileName.description: With run: the name of the file its output becomes.

mimeType.description: The file's media type; else it follows from the name's extension.

attach.description: Gives a file input its files: fixtures (`file`), or what a helper writes to its standard output (`run`, as `fileName`). Where it finds something else, it is pressed and the files go to the file chooser it opens.
attach.$comment: attach takes file (fixtures) or run (a helper), one of them

key.description: Presses a key on the focused element.

waitUrl.description: Waits until the address matches this glob.

waitText.description: Waits until this text is shown.

waitResponse.description: Waits for a response from an address that matches this glob, of this status when it says.

download.description: The download the last step started, waited for, saved and checked: what the file holds. `true` checks only that one came.

name.description: A glob of the file's name.

size.description: Its size in bytes, or { min, max }.

type.description: What kind of file it is, by its content.

text.description: A text the file holds. A text between slashes is a regular expression.

sheet.description: Of an xlsx workbook, the sheet the table is read from.

rows.description: How many rows the table has after its header.

columns.description: The header, as a list, or how many columns there are.

cells.description: Cells and what each holds: { row, column, equals } or { cell, equals }.

row.description: The row after the header, from 1.

column.description: The header's text, or the column's number from 1.

resize.description: The window of the person acting, from here on: a phone turned, a window made narrow.

run.description: A command and its arguments, as a list, run with no shell.

expect.description: With run: what the command's output must contain.

as.description: Done in this account's own browser context, opened and signed in on first use: a step another person takes.

action.description: One thing the replay does: one of goto, reload, click, fill, attach, key, waitUrl, waitText, waitResponse, download, resize and run, which may carry `as`.
